newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Britain's Foreign Secretary to visit Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Foreign Secretary to visit Vietnam.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind will visit Vietnam this week to discuss growing ties with Hanoi and plans to empty Hong Kong's camps of Vietnamese boatpeople by the middle of next year.

Diplomats at the British embassy in Hanoi said on Wednesday that Rifkind, who is in the region accompanying a Royal visit, will arrive late on Friday for talks with his Vietnamese counterpart, Nguyen Manh Cam, before leaving the next day.

He is expected to discuss broad commercial issues, including British bids for involvement in a $300 million, 390 km (240 mile) gas pipeline linking the Nam Con Son offshore field to Vietnam's southern coast.
Britain also hopes to clear boatpeople camps in Hong Kong before the colony's return to Chinese rule in mid-1997.
At the present rate of return -- around 1,600 people per month -- the task is possible.
There are around 12,000 boatpeople left in Hong Kong, the last of a wave of people who began fleeing the country by sea following the end of the Vietnam War in 1975.
Two-way trade with Vietnam is around $257 million a year and Britain ranks 13th among foreign investors in the country, with $485 million earmarked for 19 projects.
